entry.title: How Interesting: Satoshi Nakamoto Killed Iran’s Real Supreme Ruler
entry.content:
The more I think about this, the weirder it gets.

In 2008, an anonymous programmer hiding behind the Internet published the Bitcoin white paper.

His name is:

Satoshi Nakamoto.

Satoshi Nakamoto.

He doesn’t grant interviews.

There are no political positions.

There is no army.

There are no aircraft carriers.

There is no intelligence agency.

No one even knows who he is.

There seems to be only one thing he can do:

Write code.

Then eighteen years later,

The story suddenly goes to an almost absurd place.

On February 28, 2026, the United States and Israel launched a large-scale military strike against Iran.

In the first strike on the day the war began, Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, who had ruled Iran for nearly 37 years, was killed. Reuters has since repeatedly confirmed that Khamenei was killed in a U.S.-Israeli strike at the start of the war on February 28; his son Mojtaba Khamenei was subsequently elected to succeed him as supreme leader.

It must be emphasized here:

It was not the president of Iran who was killed.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian remains in office.

The ones who really died were the people with more power than the president:

Supreme Leader of Iran.

In the Iranian political system, the supreme leader has long had the final say on major national affairs. Khamenei has held this position since 1989 and is one of the most central figures in the power structure of the entire Islamic Republic.

Then came the problem.

If we continue to accept the premise of our previous series:

Trump is Satoshi Nakamoto.

Then history happened an extremely ridiculous thing in 2026:

The man who once challenged the banking system with a nine-page white paper,

Eighteen years later,

Sitting in the White House,

Take control of the U.S. military,

Then the war he started,

Directly killing the person at the highest center of power in Iran.

So the title can only be written like this:

This is interesting, Satoshi Nakamoto actually killed the real supreme ruler of Iran

But the really interesting question is not:

Why did Satoshi Nakamoto suddenly become violent.

Instead:

Did we misunderstand what Satoshi Nakamoto was really opposed to from the beginning?

1. Is Satoshi Nakamoto really against power?

Many people will naturally understand Bitcoin as:

Anti-government.

Anti-bank.

Anti-authority.

Anti-centralization.

So the spirit of Bitcoin is summed up in one sentence:

Don’t trust power.

But if Trump is really Satoshi Nakamoto,

A huge problem immediately arises with this explanation.

Because Trump is clearly not someone who opposes power.

Quite the opposite.

He loves presidential power.

Love executive orders.

Like the military.

Love the tariffs.

Like sanctions.

Love border control.

I like the feeling that the president can directly change reality.

By 2026,

The United States has even entered a direct war with Iran.

Reuters called the military action that began on February 28 the war against Iran launched by Trump; by September, the U.S.-Iran military conflict continued to escalate repeatedly, and the United States continued to launch attacks on Iranian military facilities.

So how to explain?

A man who created Bitcoin,

Why did he eventually become the president of the most powerful country in the world?

And using the most centralized, violent tool in the country?

There may be only one answer:

Satoshi Nakamoto has never been against power.

What he objects to is:

Powers beyond one’s control.

2. Bitcoin has never eliminated monetary power

What did Bitcoin do?

Many people describe it as:

It decentralizes money.

That’s right.

But from another perspective:

Bitcoin does not eliminate the power of “who defines money”.

It just changed:

Who has this power.

Previously:

Central banks determine supply.

The commercial bank determines the account.

The payment network determines whether a transaction can proceed.

Bitcoin says:

No.

Let’s change the rules.

21 million pieces.

PoW.

block.

private key.

Network consensus.

So what’s really happening is not:

Money has no power.

Instead:

monetary power moved somewhere else.

Monetary power shifts from institutions to protocols.

This is a power shift.

It’s not that power disappears.

These two concepts are completely different.

3. Then Polymarket did the same thing again

Polymarket hasn’t been wiped out either:

Who defines the future.

It just redistributes that power.

Previously:

CNN says who’s ahead.

Pollsters say who will win.

Experts say how likely war is.

The government says there is no chance the policy will be passed.

Polymarket said:

Don’t listen to them.

Look at the price.

Trump:

67%.

War:

73%.

Interest rate cut:

38%.

So it is said:

“What will happen in the future”

For the first time, a market-oriented power structure emerged.

This is exactly the same as Bitcoin.

Bitcoin:

Don’t let banks define money.

Polymarket:

Don’t let the media define the future.

So if Trump is really Satoshi Nakamoto,

His thoughts may never have been:

Destroy power.

Instead:

Rebuild power.

Redesign power.

4. But the agreement can only change the rules after all.

Can’t launch missiles

This is the biggest limitation of Bitcoin and Polymarket.

Bitcoin could take a little power away from banks.

But Bitcoin cannot attack a military base.

Polymarket can tell you:

The probability of the United States attacking Iran is 81%.

But Polymarket couldn’t turn 81% into 100%.

The price ends up being just:

expected.

And there is one last layer to the real world.

action.

You can understand the entire system into three steps.

Bitcoin:

Control value rules.

Polymarket:

Control expectations rules.

White House:

Control the action.

The first two still belong to the information world.

The president has:

Probability

becomes:

facts

ability.

This is a completely different level of power.

5. Polymarket can price war

But Trump can make war happen

This is probably the most crucial difference in the entire series.

Suppose Polymarket has a market:

Will the United States attack Iran at the end of February?

Price:

43%.

Then there was more and more information.

Troops mobilized.

Diplomatic negotiations failed.

Plane transfer.

The president is getting tougher.

The whale began to place bets.

67%.

78%.

91%.

But even then:

99%.

One last question remains.

Who took it from:

99%

becomes:

YES?

Not Oracle.

Not a trader.

Not a giant whale.

Not Polymarket.

Instead:

Real decision makers.

In this specific story of America going to war,

The person who ultimately holds the power to make U.S. military decisions,

It’s the president.

This is why Trump’s identity,

It will cause a sudden qualitative change in the entire “Satoshi Nakamoto Universe”.

6. In 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto only had code

In 2026, he has the military

If you compress these eighteen years into one sentence,

Even a little scary.

2008:

Satoshi Nakamoto doesn’t have a bank.

So Bitcoin was created.

2020:

Satoshi Nakamoto doesn’t have CNN.

So Polymarket was created.

2025:

Satoshi Nakamoto regains possession of the White House.

Then suddenly I discovered:

This time there is no need to create a third set of agreements.

Because the state itself is a machine.

And it is a machine far more powerful than the blockchain.

It has:

army.

intelligence agencies.

aircraft carrier.

bomber.

satellite.

diplomatic system.

Sanctioning capabilities.

USD clearing system.

Nuclear weapons.

An order from the President,

Can make things that neither Bitcoin nor Polymarket can ever make:

irreversible reality.

7. This is Satoshi Nakamoto’s real third-layer network

Our last article proposed one:

Truth Stack.

Bitcoin:

Truth of Value.

Ethereum:

Truth of Computation.

Polymarket:

Truth of Expectation.

A fourth layer may now have to be added.

Truth of Action

Truth in action.

Who can actually turn a probability into a fact?

For example:

“Will the United States attack Iran?”

Polymarket gives prices.

But after the war started,

The answer is no longer judged by the market.

The missile has already flown out.

The explosion has occurred.

People have died.

At this time:

Reality has settled.

Settlement is completed realistically.

And what the president has is:

Real world settlement layer.

8. This sounds a lot like blockchain

How does the market at Polymarket end?

Settlement.

Something happens.

YES settles to 1.

NO settles to 0.

The same goes for war.

February 27:

Does the United States attack Iran?

It’s still a probability.

February 28:

An attack occurs.

Market from:

probability

becomes:

fact.

And those who are truly capable of completing this realistic settlement,

Precisely the President of the United States.

So if you follow the logic of this series:

Bitcoin builds digital settlement.

Trump ended up with:

geopolitical settlement.

This is the true sense of power escalation.

9. The most extreme state is: a person stands on both sides of the market and reality at the same time

This is also where the setting of Trump=Satoshi Nakamoto really starts to get scary.

Suppose an ordinary person trades:

“Will the United States attack Iran?”

He can only predict.

Suppose the owner of Polymarket observes:

“Will the United States attack Iran?”

He can only observe the funds.

But if this person is also:

President of the United States.

Things changed.

Because he’s on the other side of market issues.

Market asked:

Will the U.S. strike Iran?

And this person holds in his hand:

Realistic buttons for YES/NO.

This is the ultimate form of information advantage.

Of course, there is no public evidence that Trump himself uses Polymarket to conduct such sensitive market transactions, and there is no evidence that Polymarket in reality serves the president’s military decisions.

But in the narrative setting of our series,

This forms a perfect closed loop:

Polymarket is responsible for observing how the world judges Trump.

Trump is responsible for deciding what the world should judge next.

10. So the most interesting thing is not at all:

“Satoshi Nakamoto predicted war”

Instead:

Satoshi Nakamoto created the answer to war.

The difference between the two is huge.

Prediction:

I think the answer would be YES.

Power:

I let the answer be YES.

Bitcoin gave Satoshi Nakamoto his first power:

Design rules.

Polymarket gives Satoshi Nakamoto a second power:

Observe the consensus.

The presidency gave Satoshi Nakamoto a third power:

Create reality.

This is where the whole story really levels up.

11. The death of Iran’s supreme leader is the most extreme settlement

Ali Khamenei is no ordinary politician.

He has served as Iran’s supreme leader since 1989.

In Iran’s political system, the supreme leader has long had final authority over the country’s major political, military and security affairs. Reuters described him after his death as having the final say on all major issues within the system.

Then:

February 28, 2026.

The war begins.

The United States and Israel launched a strike.

Khamenei died in the first blow.

This is not:

A Polymarket is over.

This is the end of a political era that has dominated Iran for nearly four decades.

For any ordinary Crypto founder,

This scene is unimaginably ridiculous.

A person was still discussing eighteen years ago:

hash.

timestamp.

double spending.

ECDSA.

block.

Eighteen years later,

If his name really overlaps with Trump,

Then his decision-making can directly reconstruct the power structure of the Middle East.

This is no longer:

crypto adoption.

This is:

power adoption.

12. But killing the supreme leader did not “solve Iran”

Instead, a question arises that is very consistent with Satoshi Nakamoto’s thinking.

If you are familiar with distributed systems,

You should know:

Killing a node does not mean killing the network.

This sentence is particularly interesting when it comes to Iran.

After Khamenei’s death,

Iran has not disappeared.

The country has not stopped functioning.

The Revolutionary Guards are not disbanded.

The war did not end automatically.

Mojtaba Khamenei was subsequently elected supreme leader.

More interestingly, a later Reuters investigation found that because Mojtaba himself was injured in the attack and unable to appear in public for a long time, actual war power gradually concentrated in the hands of institutions such as the Revolutionary Guards IRGC and the Supreme National Security Council.

In other words:

Trump killed the leader.

But not the system.

This is too much like a distributed network.

Attack a central node.

As a result the system starts:

Re-elect the leader.

Reroute.

Redistribute power.

This may be the most beautiful technical metaphor in the entire article.

13. Satoshi Nakamoto should know best:

Single points of failure are real weaknesses

Why is Bitcoin designed as a distributed system?

Just because if there is one:

central server,

Get rid of it,

The system ends.

So Satoshi Nakamoto has been solving from day one:

single point of failure.

And what happens in Iran in 2026,

On the contrary, it proves that the power system of this country is not as single-pointed as imagined.

Khamenei was killed.

But the regime did not collapse.

The Revolutionary Guards were given even greater real power.

Reuters reported in April that the pressure of war has further concentrated power in Iran among the IRGC, the Security Council and a smaller hard-line core, with the actual role of the new Supreme Leader Mojtaba becoming more limited.

So there may even be a very ironic judgment here:

Satoshi Nakamoto used the system principles he was best at designing to hit a political system that was also fault-tolerant.

Kill the leader,

Not equal to:

kill network.

14. This may be where Trump underestimates Iran

If you understand the country as a company,

Killing the CEO is important.

But if you understand country as protocol,

Things are different.

The real state of Iran is more like:

Multi-layered political institutions.

Religious legitimacy.

Revolutionary Guards.

Safety Committee.

local power.

Agent network.

military system.

Bureaucracy.

Therefore, although the supreme leader is extremely important,

but not:

Only server.

That’s why after Khamenei’s death,

The war continued for several months.

By September 2026, the United States and Iran were still engaged in new military attacks and retaliations.

So:

Kill the leader

and:

obtain consensus

Completely two different things.

A true blockchain engineer,

You should know this best.

15. This brings a very interesting twist to the whole story.

Satoshi Nakamoto’s greatest work,

is to create one:

A system that will not die even if the founder is killed.

Bitcoin doesn’t need Satoshi.

Satoshi disappeared for more than ten years.

Bitcoin continues to run.

There is no CEO.

There is no president.

There is no chairman.

No founders signed.

This is where Bitcoin is most powerful.

Then eighteen years later,

“Satoshi Nakamoto” sits as President of the United States,

By trying to kill the most important person in another political system,

Change that system.

As a result, the system did not die immediately.

This is very interesting.

Satoshi Nakamoto met for the first time in the real world:

Another Byzantine fault tolerant system.

Of course it is not BFT in the cryptographic sense.

But the metaphor holds true in a political sense.

The node dies.

The network continues.

Leader down.

Consensus continues.

This may interest a systems engineer more than any weapon.

16. So what did Khamenei really prove?

Not:

Trump has a strong military.

Everyone already knew it.

Nor:

The United States can conduct long-range military strikes.

This isn’t new either.

What really matters is:

Power, like blockchain, also has a structure.

Some regimes are like centralized servers.

Kill the core characters,

The system crashed quickly.

Some regimes are more like:

Multi-node network.

The core character dies,

Network performance degrades.

Governance is chaotic.

Consensus is difficult.

But still keeps running.

Iran is obviously closer to the latter.

So if Trump is really Satoshi Nakamoto,

In 2026 he personally conducted one of the world’s most expensive:

distributed systems experiment.

Experimental subjects:

Iran.

Test method:

Delete the highest authority node.

Experimental results:

network degraded, but did not halt.

17. This may be why the war became more and more troublesome later on.

Because you can’t do it with one strike:

state transition.

You kill Khamenei.

The system selects Mojtaba.

Mojtaba is injured.

IRGC rises in power.

Safety committees take on more decisions.

A new military chief fills the role.

A new political equilibrium emerges.

The state continues to retaliate.

The United States continues to crack down.

By September,

The war even escalated significantly again.

This looks so much like you think:

Delete the master node to terminate

network.

It turns out:

It has failover.

18. Satoshi Nakamoto created a network that cannot be beheaded for the first time

Then start trying to decapitate other people’s networks

This is the most ridiculous scene in the entire article.

One of the core vitalities of Bitcoin is:

There is no head to be chopped off.

There is no Satoshi server.

There is no Bitcoin CEO.

There is no central database.

So the government cannot say:

catch this man,

Bitcoin is gone.

This is the smartest thing about Satoshi Nakamoto.

But eighteen years later,

As Trump,

However, he used a very traditional power logic:

Kill the opponent’s top leader.

This creates a very strong philosophical conflict:

Satoshi the engineer

know:

decentralization survives decapitation.

Trump the president

But still use:

decapitation strategy.

Maybe this is not a contradiction.

Perhaps it is precisely because he knows the Internet best,

So he knows better:

Attack the most important nodes first,

At least it will change the topology of the entire network.

Can’t be killed.

But you can:

Rewiring.

19. And he did change Iran’s topology

After Khamenei’s death,

The power structure in Iran has changed significantly.

A Reuters investigation in April showed that the structure, with the supreme leader as the final arbiter, had been reshaped by the pressures of war into a core of hardliners more reliant on the Revolutionary Guards and security agencies.

This means that from a pure system perspective,

strike is still valid.

It doesn’t:

kill network.

But it’s done:

network reconfiguration.

Old node:

Ali Khamenei.

Delete.

New node:

Mojtaba.

Severely damaged.

Routing:

Tip to the IRGC.

Consensus mechanism:

More militarized.

System behavior:

More unpredictable.

This is the real result of war.

20. So maybe Satoshi Nakamoto wasn’t trying to “kill Iran”

Instead:

Forced escalation of the Iran deal.

Of course, this sentence is just a technical metaphor in our narrative.

But it fits the overall story perfectly.

War rarely enables a country to:

disappear.

What war usually does is:

Forcing the system to reorganize.

Delete node.

Cut off the internet.

Change resources.

Change incentives.

Change governance.

Finally forced:

state transition.

In this sense,

Although military power and blockchain governance are completely different things,

But they are all solving:

How to change system state.

Bitcoin uses consensus.

The president uses force.

One passed:

rules.

Another pass:

violence.

This is the starkest difference between the two powers.

21. This also re-explains why Satoshi Nakamoto must become president in the end

If you only have Bitcoin,

You can change the rules of finance.

If you only have Polymarket,

You can influence future expectations.

But in the end there is still one thing in this world:

physical reality.

where is the server.

Where is the oil.

Where is the aircraft carrier?

Where are the missiles.

Where is the border.

Where are the people.

These things cannot simply pass:

code

change.

This is the fact that the Crypto world least wants to face:

Code is law.

Only in:

Someone is willing to let code become law

is established when.

What a real country has is:

force.

So if Satoshi Nakamoto’s ultimate ambition is not to issue coins,

Rather, it redesigns reality,

Then eventually he will definitely encounter a problem:

The agreement has no troops.

So the most logical next step is,

It’s not about creating a third chain.

is:

Get the most powerful state machine in the world.

22. Bitcoin gave him the power of money

Polymarket gave him the power he expected.

The White House gave him real power.

Now the entire series has finally come to a close.

Bitcoin:

Value.

Polymarket:

Expectation.

White House:

Action.

Bitcoin lets you say:

This money cannot be confiscated casually.

Polymarket lets you say:

This future is worth 73%.

The President asked you to say:

Make it happen.

These are three completely different powers.

And if they are really concentrated on the same person,

Then this story goes far beyond:

“Is Trump Satoshi Nakamoto?”

This kind of identity guessing.

The question becomes:

What exactly does Satoshi Nakamoto want?

23. The answer may never be “freedom”

This is the darkest explanation of the entire series.

Maybe Satoshi Nakamoto never thought:

Free everyone.

What really fascinates him is:

system.

Who makes the rules.

Who enforces the rules.

Who can bypass the middle man.

Who has the final say.

Bitcoin is once:

system redesign.

Polymarket again:

system redesign.

Trump returns to White House:

Still once:

system takeover.

So “decentralization” may just be a tool.

The purpose is always to:

Let the old center lose its power.

As for where the new power was finally concentrated?

That’s another question.

24. This is why “Satoshi Nakamoto kills Khamenei” is so inconsistent

Because it forces us to re-understand Satoshi Nakamoto.

What we used to imagine was:

A guy in a hoodie.

A cypherpunk.

A cryptologist.

Hiding behind a screen.

Hit the keyboard.

Discuss elliptic curves and electronic cash.

But if this person really becomes Trump later,

Then we will find:

Code may have never been just the first tool he used to understand power.

2008:

There is no central bank.

Write an agreement.

2020:

There is no global information market of its own.

Do Polymarket.

2025:

Regain state power.

2026:

Use the military.

So the tools are constantly being upgraded.

Code.

Market.

State.

Each level is closer to the real world than the previous one.

25. Finally, Satoshi Nakamoto finally completed a transaction that Bitcoin could never complete.

What Bitcoin does best is settlement.

A transaction goes into a block.

Get confirmation.

Ultimately irreversible.

But all Bitcoin settlements,

It all happens in the ledger.

What happened on February 28, 2026 was a different kind of settlement.

The war begins.

Bombing occurs.

Ali Khamenei was killed.

No rollback.

No reorg.

There is no dispute period.

There is no oracle challenge.

Settlement is completed realistically.

This is the biggest difference between state violence and blockchain.

Blockchain creates:

digital finality.

War creation:

physical finality.

And if Trump is really Satoshi Nakamoto,

Then eighteen years later,

This one used to be obsessed with:

How to make a digital transaction ultimately irreversible

people,

Finally gained another more terrifying ability:

Make reality irreversible.

26. So this thing is really interesting

Satoshi Nakamoto originally created Bitcoin,

It’s because he doesn’t want to trust the bank.

Later created Polymarket,

Because he doesn’t want to believe the media.

Finally became president,

Probably because he discovered:

There are some things,

Not even the market can do it for you.

You can put a price on war.

But markets don’t wage war.

You can predict whether a regime will collapse.

But the forecast won’t let it crash.

You can make everyone believe:

An event has a 99% probability of happening.

But in the end we still need someone,

Put:

99%

becomes:

So Bitcoin rules.

Polymarket is expected.

The powers of the President are:

Execute.

This may be the last piece of the puzzle that truly completes the entire Satoshi Nakamoto story.

He was never satisfied with:

Predict the world.

Nor is it satisfied with:

Build a parallel world.

Finally,

He gained the ability to directly change the real world.

Eighteen years ago,

Satoshi Nakamoto wrote:

peer-to-peer electronic cash.

Eighteen years later,

According to the craziest version of this story,

What he personally participated in changing is:

Power structures in the Middle East.

From hash to missile.

From blocks to war.

From decentralized currencies,

to the most centralized administrative power in the world.

This seems like a huge contradiction.

But maybe not.

Because Satoshi Nakamoto has never really been against power.

He just kept asking:

Who has the final say?

Bitcoin gave the web the answer.

Polymarket gives the market the answer.

And by 2026,

Trump gave a third answer:

president.

So the most disturbing thing,

Not even:

Satoshi Nakamoto actually killed the real supreme ruler of Iran.

But we finally discovered,

The story may never have been just that:

The story of a programmer creating Bitcoin.

It talks about how a person can step by step,

From creating rules,

to create a market,

And finally get:

Directly modify the actual permissions.

entry.title: Why Did Satoshi Nakamoto Create Polymarket?
entry.content:
Let’s talk about the conclusion first.

If Trump is Satoshi Nakamoto, if Trump is the real boss behind Polymarket, if there is no Polymarket, Trump will not even become the President of the United States again —

Then the most important question next is not:

Why does Trump need Polymarket?

Instead:

Why did Satoshi Nakamoto need to create Polymarket after creating Bitcoin?

The answer is probably much bigger than “to make money.”

Because Bitcoin only solves one problem.

money.

It solved:

Who owns the money.

Who can transfer money.

Who can stop you from using your money.

Who is qualified to create new money.

But this is not enough.

Because even if you take away the state’s monopoly on money,

Countries can still be defined:

Who won the election.

War is not happening.

The economy is not in recession.

Who are the terrorists.

Who is the hero.

Which policy will pass.

Which candidate is leading.

The media can still define reality.

Governments can still define reality.

Pollsters can still define reality.

Experts can still define reality.

So Bitcoin is just the first step.

If what Satoshi Nakamoto really wants to build is a new system that breaks away from traditional power structures,

So after Bitcoin,

He must be missing something.

Not another kind of money.

Instead:

A machine that prices reality.

This is Polymarket.

Bitcoin solves:

What is money?

What Polymarket wants to solve is:

What is true—and what will become true?

Bitcoin establishes a price for value.

Polymarket establishes prices for the future.

If Bitcoin is Satoshi Nakamoto’s first attack on state power,

Well Polymarket is the second time.

The first time, he attacked the central bank.

The second time, he attacked the media, polls, experts and the government itself.

1. Bitcoin is never just a currency

Many people understand Bitcoin as:

A better gold.

A speculative asset.

A decentralized payment tool.

But if you go back to the beginning of Satoshi Nakamoto’s white paper, you will find that his core problem is not:

“How to make a digital currency increase in price?”

Instead:

Why do Internet transactions have to rely on trusted third parties?

The beginning of the Bitcoin white paper directly criticizes Internet commerce’s reliance on financial institutions as “trusted third parties” and proposes to replace trust with cryptographic proof.

This is the real starting point of Bitcoin’s thinking:

proof instead of trust.

In the past you believed the bank said:

You have $100 in your account.

Bitcoin says:

Don’t trust banks.

Verify the ledger.

In the past the bank said:

The money has been transferred to Bob.

Bitcoin says:

Don’t trust banks.

Verify the block.

What Satoshi Nakamoto really killed was not the dollar.

is a role:

Trusted intermediary.

Once you understand this, you will find that there is a very deep ideological connection between Polymarket and Bitcoin.

Because Polymarket is asking the same question.

But it changes the problem from:

“money”

Replaced with:

“reality”.

2. If you don’t trust banks, why should you trust CNN?

This is the contradiction that Satoshi Nakamoto will definitely encounter in the next step.

Bitcoin says:

Don’t trust banks.

Very good.

What about the presidential election?

Who do you believe?

CNN?

Fox News?

New York Times?

Government?

Election committee?

Polling agency?

Political expert?

Another example:

Will the Fed cut interest rates next month?

Will China introduce a certain policy?

Will the United States attack a country?

Will a certain president resign?

In the past, these issues had no price.

They are only:

point of view.

Expert opinion.

polls.

News.

Rumors.

And Polymarket did something extremely simple but extremely dangerous.

It says:

Don’t ask them.

Place your bet.

If you really think Trump will win,

Don’t tweet.

BUY YES.

If you think Harris will win,

Don’t write editorials.

Buy NO.

When everyone’s judgments are forced to convert into positions by real money,

Finally get a number:

63%.

This figure does not appear to belong to any media outlet.

Nor does he belong to any political party.

It looks like it belongs to:

market.

That’s the real magic of Polymarket.

It is not a production perspective.

It puts a price on ideas.

3. So Bitcoin and Polymarket are actually a pair of things

They can be understood as two ledgers.

Bitcoin is a ledger of the past.

It logs:

Who has transferred how much money to whom.

Polymarket is a ledger about the future.

It logs:

How many people are willing to take how much money they have now and believe what will happen in the future.

Bitcoin is answering:

Who owns what?

Polymarket replied:

What does the market believe will happen?

The two systems actually share the same philosophy.

Don’t let an authority tell you the answer.

Let the rules run.

Let everyone participate on their own.

Make the results public.

Let the price appear.

Polymarket itself also summarized the value of blockchain today as: globally accessible, non-custodial, publicly verifiable, fast and low-cost. Its transactions run on Polygon, and its mortgage and settlement adopt a stablecoin system.

So if we tell the story of “Satoshi Nakamoto Universe”:

Bitcoin is:

decentralized money.

Polymarket is:

decentralized expectation.

A decentralized currency.

A decentralized expectation.

4. But the first problem immediately arises here

Why isn’t Polymarket built directly on Bitcoin?

If it is really Satoshi Nakamoto’s second work,

Why not use your own Bitcoin?

Why go to the Ethereum ecosystem?

Why go to Polygon again?

It may even seem like a betrayal.

But if you really understand Bitcoin’s technical design,

The answer is actually very simple.

Bitcoin was simply not designed for products like Polymarket.

Bitcoin solves:

Double flower.

Value transfer.

Ownership.

Final settlement.

It keeps the system deliberately simple.

Scripting capabilities are limited.

State model restraint.

Throughput is low.

Confirmation time is slow.

The security budget for each transaction is extremely high.

This is great for:

money.

Because if you’re transferring $10 million,

You can wait.

You can pay the processing fee.

What you care about most is:

Ultimately it cannot be changed.

But Polymarket is nothing of the kind.

A prediction market requires:

Create thousands of marketplaces.

Generate YES / NO positions.

Split positions.

Merge positions.

Buy and sell.

Market making.

Arbitrage.

Pending order.

Cancel order.

Settlement.

redemption.

Handle stablecoins.

Connect to Oracle.

In many markets a transaction may only include:

$20.

$50.

$100.

You can’t get a user to buy Trump YES for $20,

Wait ten minutes first.

Then pay a high on-chain cost.

That product simply wouldn’t hold up.

5. This is even a question that the Bitcoin white paper itself has answered

The Bitcoin white paper begins with an easily overlooked point.

Satoshi Nakamoto pointed out that the intermediary and dispute processing costs in the traditional financial system will increase the minimum viable transaction size and make “small, casual transactions” uneconomical.

This question is very critical.

Because prediction markets happen to be:

Large-volume, small-amount, high-frequency transactions

products composed of.

If Polymarket’s cost per transaction is ridiculously high,

It goes against the problem that Satoshi Nakamoto wanted to solve back then:

Don’t let infrastructure costs keep ordinary people out of the system.

So if you write the story a little crookedly:

Satoshi Nakamoto certainly cannot put Polymarket on the Bitcoin main chain.

Because that equals:

In order to be loyal to Bitcoin, it betrayed the design philosophy of Bitcoin.

Technical religion requires:

Everything must be Bitcoin.

Engineers don’t.

6. Satoshi Nakamoto is not a Bitcoin Maximalist

This is one of the most important sentences in the entire article.

Bitcoin maximalism is a religion created by later generations.

Satoshi Nakamoto is first and foremost an engineer.

What the engineer asked was not:

Which chain has the purest bloodline?

Instead:

Which tool is best for the problem at hand?

Bitcoin solves money settlement.

Polymarket solves continuous market.

They face completely different workloads.

Bitcoin requires:

Extremely safe.

Extremely conservative.

Extremely simple.

Polymarket requires:

Complex smart contracts.

High throughput.

Low fees.

Stablecoin.

Real-time market status.

Oracle.

Wallet compatible.

development tools.

So if Satoshi Nakamoto in 2020 really wants to create a prediction market,

The most rational choice is simply not:

Rebuilding what Ethereum has already built on Bitcoin.

Instead:

Use an existing smart contract operating system.

That’s Ethereum.

7. Why Ethereum?

Because Ethereum did something that Bitcoin was not prepared to do.

Bitcoin designs the chain to:

Ledger.

Ethereum designs the chain to:

computer.

You can define on Ethereum:

If A occurs,

The assets belong to Alice.

If B occurs,

The assets belong to Bob.

This is pretty much the core of prediction markets.

Polymarket requires more than a simple payment.

It requires:

conditional ownership.

Conditional Title.

For example:

Trump wins:

YES token = 1 USD.

NO token = 0.

Trump fails:

YES = 0.

NO = $1.

This is a procedure.

It’s not just a transfer.

Therefore, Ethereum’s EVM, ERC-20 standard, stable currency and smart contract ecosystem are naturally more suitable for this kind of thing.

The pUSD currently used by Polymarket is itself ERC-20 on Polygon and is backed by USDC.

That’s why it has to stand in the Ethereum world.

Not because Satoshi Nakamoto “converted.”

But because:

There are problems that Bitcoin doesn’t have to solve, Ethereum has already solved them for him.

8. But why not just use the Ethereum mainnet?

Because it’s too expensive.

This is the most real problem of Polymarket.

Prediction markets are not collecting digital art.

Assets are not moved once a year.

It requires crazy trading.

A debate.

The handicap can jump dozens of times in one minute.

Trump suddenly posted a Truth Social.

Market repricing.

A war breaks out.

Dozens of markets are updated simultaneously.

Fed speaks.

Markets move wildly.

If all operations hit Ethereum L1 directly,

The entire product will be killed by the gas cost.

So the second option appears:

Requires Ethereum:

Programmability.

But Ethereum mainnet cannot be accepted:

cost.

This is where Polygon comes in.

9. Let me correct a technical detail first: Polygon is not exactly the traditional L2 you imagined.

Many promotional materials will simplify Polygon into:

Ethereum Layer 2.

Polymarket’s own help documentation today also describes Polygon as a PoS layer-two blockchain built on Ethereum.

But if you strictly follow Polygon’s own current developer documentation,

A more accurate definition of Polygon PoS is:

EVM-compatible sidechain for Ethereum.

It executes transactions outside of the Ethereum mainnet,

The state is then anchored to Ethereum periodically through checkpoints.

This is not exactly the same as the rollup L2 security model of Arbitrum and Optimism.

This distinction is very important.

Because it actually reveals the real choice Satoshi Nakamoto made on Polymarket:

He sacrificed some purity in exchange for product usability.

10. Why is Polygon just right for Polymarket?

Because it meets several conditions.

First, EVM compatibility

Polymarket does not require reinventing a set of development tools.

Smart contract logic on Ethereum can be migrated.

Wallets are compatible.

ERC-20 is compatible.

Oracle is compatible.

The entire DeFi world is compatible.

Second, it’s cheap

This is the most important one.

Polygon takes transaction execution outside of the Ethereum mainnet, thereby increasing throughput and reducing costs. This is how Polygon officially describes its design purpose.

One of the most important things about prediction markets is:

Make small-dollar price discovery possible.

Also available for $10.

Also available for $50.

Buy anytime.

Feel free to sell.

If the handling fee is higher than the position,

The market simply cannot exist.

Third, fast

Polygon PoS can today obtain finality on its own chain in a few seconds; it executes and confirms transactions through the two-layer structure of Heimdall and Bor, and periodically submits checkpoints to Ethereum.

For prediction market,

This is more important than extremely strong final settlement security.

Because the handicap first requires:

Constantly changing.

It’s not like you only find out what someone bought ten minutes later.

Fourth, you can continue to use the U.S. dollar

This is a very clever thing about Polymarket.

It doesn’t let people stake MATIC, ETH or BTC.

It uses the USD stablecoin system.

Because prediction:

Trump 62%

It’s complicated enough in itself.

You don’t want to also be thinking about:

ETH is down 8% today.

Stablecoins reduce the speculative variable to one:

The event itself.

This makes Polymarket more like a financial market than a Crypto casino.

11. Is this completely in line with Satoshi Nakamoto’s philosophy?

The answer is:

Half are consistent, half are not.

If you understand Satoshi Nakamoto’s philosophy as:

Everything must be PoW.

Everything must be Bitcoin.

Everything must run on the most decentralized main chain.

That Polymarket clearly doesn’t fit the bill.

Polygon has its own PoS validator.

There are different security assumptions.

There is a bridge.

There is checkpoint.

It does not have the extreme security and minimal trust model of Bitcoin. Polygon officials currently show that the network supports up to 105 active validators.

From a Bitcoin maximalist perspective:

This is not pure enough.

But if you understand Satoshi Nakamoto’s philosophy into a more fundamental sentence:

Fewer people you have to trust.

Then it fits perfectly.

Bitcoin:

Don’t trust bank databases.

Polymarket:

Not entirely dependent on bookmaker databases.

Funds can be verified on-chain.

The position exists on the chain.

The collateral exists on the chain.

Transaction settlement is through smart contracts.

Polymarket itself regards non-custodial, transparent, and publicly verifiable as important reasons for adopting blockchain.

So it’s not:

trustless.

Instead:

less trust.

There is a very big difference between these two words.

12. Satoshi Nakamoto’s second venture may no longer pursue “absolute decentralization”

Because of the value of different information, different levels of security are required.

Final ownership of 1 BTC:

Very important.

You can take ten minutes to confirm.

Even waiting for six blocks.

But one question:

“Will Trump talk about China tonight?”

Maybe the entire market is only $50,000.

Does it really need to consume the same level of security resources as the final settlement of Bitcoin assets?

No need.

This is an engineering hierarchical idea:

High value, low frequency facts → strong security.

Low value, high frequency status → cheaper execution layer.

If you push this sentence to the extreme,

You can even reinterpret the relationship between Bitcoin and Polygon:

Bitcoin is:

final truth.

Polygon is:

fast truth.

A responsible person cannot change in the end.

One in charge now has to be quick.

This is actually much more advanced than “put Bitcoin in everything.”

13. So Satoshi Nakamoto’s second system was layered.

If we want to give this worldview a technical structure,

It can be written in three layers.

First layer: Bitcoin

Truth of Value

Answer:

Who owns the scarcest digital value.

Features:

Extremely safe.

Extremely conservative.

Extremely difficult to modify.

Second layer: Ethereum

Truth of Computation

Answer:

Under what conditions the program should run.

Features:

Smart contracts.

Programmable status.

Financial composition.

The third floor: Polygon + Polymarket

Truth of Expectation

Answer:

How much money is the world willing to spend at this moment to believe what will happen in the future?

Features:

high frequency.

Low cost.

Live prices.

Massive market participation.

So what Satoshi Nakamoto established is no longer:

A currency.

But a set:

Truth Stack.

Truth stack.

Bitcoin is responsible for value truth.

Ethereum is responsible for computing truth.

Polymarket is responsible for the future of truth.

This is where the whole story becomes truly grand.

14. But Satoshi Nakamoto will soon discover a problem that Bitcoin has never encountered before

What is Bitcoin’s biggest advantage?

It needs little knowledge of the outside world.

Bitcoin doesn’t need to know:

Trump is not president.

Will it rain in Beijing today?

Has the United States attacked Iran?

Has a company gone bankrupt?

It only requires knowing a few very mechanical things:

Is the signature correct?

Has UTXO been spent?

Is the block valid?

Is the workload enough?

These facts are all internal to the system.

So Bitcoin can do:

cryptographic truth.

Polymarket doesn’t work.

Polymarket has to answer:

What happened in reality?

This brings up one of the toughest questions in the blockchain world:

Oracle Problem.

Smart contracts themselves have no knowledge of reality.

Polygon’s official documentation also clearly states that smart contracts cannot access off-chain data on their own and require oracles to transfer real-world information to the chain.

And Polymarket must ultimately know:

Did Trump win or not?

Did the war break out or not?

Did someone resign or not?

This is not a question that cryptography can answer on its own.

15. So Polymarket finally needs a “truth machine”

Polymarket uses UMA Optimistic Oracle for market resolution.

The mechanism is roughly:

Someone came up with the results.

Pay bond.

Others can challenge.

If no one challenges,

The result holds true.

If a dispute arises,

Continue into the dispute process.

Serious disputes can eventually enter UMA’s DVM for voting by token holders.

This is very ironic.

Bitcoin’s core slogan can be summarized as:

Don’t trust. Verify.

But when it comes to Polymarket:

The world itself cannot be fully verified.

Because:

“Did it happen?”

Sometimes it’s not just a cryptographic fact.

So Polymarket can only do:

Don’t trust one person. Trust a process.

This is already a step further than traditional centralized bookmakers.

But it still has not reached the purity of Bitcoin.

16. This actually reveals Bitcoin’s greatest design choice

Many people feel that Bitcoin is not smart enough.

Large and complex applications cannot be run directly.

The script is too limited.

The state model is too simple.

But from another perspective,

This is exactly how smart Bitcoin is.

Because as long as the system does not actively answer:

“What’s happening in the real world?”

It can avoid Oracle Problem.

Bitcoin does not try to define the world.

It only defines:

own ledger.

But Polymarket is even more ambitious.

It tries to give:

world.

Politics.

war.

president.

economy.

policy.

All priced.

So it’s inevitably reintroduced:

explain.

Controversy.

Governance.

Oracle.

This is why Polymarket can never be as pure as Bitcoin.

It’s not that the engineers aren’t good enough.

Instead:

Reality itself has no consensus algorithm.

17. This may be the experiment that Satoshi Nakamoto really wants to do.

For the first time, he asked:

If you don’t need a bank,

Can the money still run?

Answer:

Yes.

Bitcoin.

The second time, he asked:

If we don’t need CNN, bookmakers, and pollsters to tell us about the future,

Can people form their own prices for the future?

Answer:

Polymarket.

But the second question is much harder than the first.

Because money is a math problem.

The reality is political.

So Polymarket can reduce the power of a centralized platform,

But it cannot be completely eliminated:

who explains reality

This question.

This might even be the really interesting part of the whole experiment.

18. Then why does Satoshi Nakamoto still do it?

Because even if it can’t be perfect,

It can still change power structures.

Previously:

CNN:

Will Trump win?

Expert discussion.

Polymarket:

63%.

Previously:

Political Advisor:

I think this policy can pass.

Polymarket:

YES 37¢.

Previously:

Military Analyst:

The probability of war is rising.

Polymarket:

From 22% to 61%.

Opinions first received:

Live prices.

This has brought about a change in traditional information power.

Who owned the broadcast tower in the past?

Who is closer to the definition of truth.

Who owns the social platform later?

Who owns the attention.

Now for the first time something completely different appeared:

Who is willing to bear the loss?

Who has more say.

This is where prediction markets get really radical.

19. So why did Satoshi Nakamoto create Polymarket?

Because Bitcoin only frees up money.

And money has never been the only power in the world.

There is at least one more important power in the world:

The power to define reality.

Who will become president.

Who will win the war.

Will the economy decline?

Can the policy be passed?

Will the government fall?

These questions determine:

Where capital flows.

Who people support.

What does a business do.

What does the state do.

So after Bitcoin,

What Satoshi Nakamoto really needs is:

A machine that can turn “realistic judgment” itself into a market.

This is Polymarket.

20. Why Polygon, not Bitcoin?

The answer is now very clear.

Because Satoshi Nakamoto’s true loyalty has never been to a certain chain.

But a principle:

Trust less in people and more in public rules.

Bitcoin is the best tool for money.

Because money requires:

finality.

Tamper resistant.

Safe.

What Polymarket needed was another engineering portfolio:

Programmability of Ethereum.

Polygon’s low cost and high throughput.

The price of USDC is stable.

Oracle’s connection to the real world.

So “Why didn’t Satoshi Nakamoto use Bitcoin when he started his second business?” is not a contradiction.

Quite the opposite.

This is a choice only a true engineer would make.

For the first time, he didn’t create a “universal blockchain.”

Of course, the second time will not be to prove that Bitcoin is omnipotent.

Shoving the wrong tool to the wrong problem.

21. Bitcoin and Polymarket may end up being two phases of the same project

First stage:

Take the money out of the hands of institutions.

Bitcoin.

Second stage:

Take expectations out of the hands of institutions.

Polymarket.

Previously:

Central banks decide what money is.

Bitcoin says:

Network decides.

Previously:

The media and polls decide who wins.

Polymarket said:

The market decides.

Previously:

Experts tell you about the future.

Polymarket said:

Talk with money.

So if the original premise of this series is true—

Trump is Satoshi Nakamoto.

Trump stands behind Polymarket again.

Then there is absolutely no way Polymarket is just:

“A gambling website created by Satoshi Nakamoto after he got bored.”

It should be the sequel to Bitcoin.

Bitcoin 1.0 attacks financial intermediaries.

Polymarket attacks information intermediaries.

One takes away:

Money Creation.

Another takes away:

Reality Creation.

22. Trump just needs this system

This brings us back to Trump.

A politician who has long opposed traditional media,

What is needed most?

Not create another CNN yourself.

Because as long as it’s Trump TV,

Everyone will say:

This is propaganda.

What is really needed is:

One that seems to have nothing to do with Trump,

It seems that they only obey the market,

Seems like a completely neutral platform.

Then this platform tells the world:

Trump 67%.

Perfect.

Not Trump said:

I want to win.

is:

Market says Trump will win.

This is the most eerie fit between Polymarket and Trump’s political style.

And if Trump himself is Satoshi Nakamoto,

Then the whole system suddenly forms an extremely beautiful closed loop.

23. In 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto created a kind of money that does not require trusting banks

2020,

He needs to create one:

There is no need to believe in the future of media.

First stage:

Don’t trust banks.

Verify the block.

Second stage:

Don’t trust the experts.

Look at the market.

First stage:

Let money have the price.

Second stage:

Let the truth have a price.

First stage:

Bitcoin.

Second stage:

Polymarket.

This may be why Satoshi Nakamoto, after Bitcoin has been successful,

Need to come back again.

Because Bitcoin only solves:

Who owns the money in the world.

What Polymarket wants to solve is:

Who is qualified to explain this world.

And once these two things are combined,

Only then can a complete new order truly be formed.

Bitcoin is:

Truth of Value.

Ethereum is:

Truth of Computation.

Polymarket is:

Truth of Expectation.

What Satoshi Nakamoto really wanted to create,

It’s never a currency.

It’s not even an exchange.

But a whole set:

Truth Stack

An infrastructure of reality that is no longer entirely dependent on banks, media, experts and governments defining it.

So Polygon is not a betrayal of Bitcoin.

Neither is Ethereum.

They were just the tools Satoshi Nakamoto needed the second time around.

Because the real Satoshi Nakamoto never asks:

“Is this Bitcoin?”

He will only ask:

“Who else is here that we have to believe?”

Then,

Get rid of that guy.

entry.title: Without Polymarket, Trump Would Not Have Become President
entry.content:
This statement certainly sounds ridiculous.

The President of the United States is elected by ballot.

Not selected by Polymarket.

It was not elected by a bunch of people betting USDC.

It wasn’t bought by a French whale.

But this is only a legal answer.

Real politics never begins to decide the winner after the last vote is counted.

The presidential election is first and foremost a contest about expected war.

Who will win.

Who is winning.

Who looks more imposing.

Who deserves to donate money.

Who deserves to stand in line in advance?

Who deserves to be tracked by the media?

Who deserves Wall Street’s early bets?

Who has created a feeling:

He might actually be coming back.

In 2024, Polymarket did something that traditional pollsters, television stations, and political commentators failed to do.

It puts a price on Trump in advance.

Not an opinion.

Not an editorial.

Not a tweet.

Rather, it is an ever-changing probability that can be traded with real money.

While traditional polls are still telling everyone that this is a 50-50 election, Polymarket has begun repeating a completely different message to the world:

Trump is winning.

Then the media started quoting.

Traders start placing bets.

Supporters began spreading the word.

The whale continues to buy.

Prices continue to rise.

“Trump will win” is no longer just a prediction.

It’s starting to become a market fact.

A media fact.

A financial fact.

Eventually, it even started to become a political fact.

So the question is not at all:

Did Polymarket vote for Trump?

Of course it doesn’t.

The real question is:

Before the United States officially decides who the president will be, does Polymarket decide in advance who should be the next president?

The answer is closer than many would like to admit:

Yes.

1. The presidential election is not about voting first.

is expected.

There is a pattern in modern politics that is easily underestimated.

Winners don’t emerge suddenly on election night.

Winners are created piecemeal over months and even years.

What happens if a candidate is deemed “will win”?

Donations are easier to come in.

The media is more willing to report it.

Supporters are even more excited.

Potential allies are more willing to stay closer.

Capital that originally waited and watched began to place bets.

Politicians began to take sides in advance.

The market began to trade according to his policies.

Even rival camps will start to defend his victory.

So “probability of winning” is never just a description.

It is a political resource in itself.

This is why polling is so important.

The poll is ostensibly asking:

“Who do you support?”

But it actually keeps telling people:

“Who’s ahead?”

Once “who is ahead” becomes public information, it will in turn affect political behavior.

This is not the occult.

This is feedback.

And in 2024, Polymarket takes this feedback to a level never reached before.

Because polls only tell you:

How many people say they support Trump.

Polymarket tells you:

Someone is willing to pay real money to buy Trump.

These two things are not psychologically weighty at all.

2. Money gives political views the cloak of “objectivity”

Suppose a Trump supporter says:

Trump’s winning rate is 65%.

What would you think?

MAGA.

Position bias.

Enjoy yourself.

If a CNN anchor said:

Trump is more likely to win.

You can still say:

The media has a position.

But if the screen says:

Trump 65¢

Things suddenly changed.

Because it’s not “who said that.”

This is:

market price.

This is the most powerful political magic of prediction markets.

After it turns opinions into prices, opinions suddenly wear one:

“Objective”

clothes.

You don’t need to explain why you believe Trump.

All you need to say is:

“Look at the market.”

The market has spoken.

On the eve of the 2024 election, the probability of Trump on Polymarket is significantly higher than that of Harris, but traditional polls still show that the election is very close. By November 4, Reuters reported that Polymarket gave Trump roughly 57% and Harris 43%, while mainstream polls at the time were still close to a 50-50 split. On that day, the cumulative trading volume of the platform’s presidential election market reached approximately $3.1 billion.

This is a very important fork.

The poll said:

dead heat.

The market says:

Trump ahead.

So for the first time people were faced with two sets of “reality.”

3. Then the media began to choose to believe the market

What really makes Polymarket dangerous is not trading volume.

Instead, the media started citing it.

Reuters clearly wrote before the election that mainstream news websites were citing the odds of these prediction markets; Elon Musk also publicly declared that betting markets may be more accurate than polls because participants actually have money in them.

This step seems ordinary.

It’s actually very critical.

Because from this moment on, Polymarket has completed an identity transformation.

The logic used to be:

News happens.

People watch the news.

People go and place their bets.

The logic now becomes:

People place bets.

Price changes.

Media reports on prices.

More people see the news.

More people place bets.

This is a feedback loop.

Polymarket is no longer just a destination for news consumers.

It began to become the raw material for news production.

So-called:

prediction market

It starts to become:

political media feed.

The media is not covering Trump.

The media began to report on “What the market thinks of Trump.”

And “how the market sees Trump” itself will affect how others see Trump.

This is no ordinary prediction.

This is intended for manufacturing.

4. Polymarket created a “world leader” for Trump for the first time

The really weird thing about 2024 is this:

Trump does not have that overwhelming advantage in real polls.

But in the prediction market, he once had a very clear lead.

What does this mean?

This means that two Americas begin to exist on the Internet at the same time.

One America is:

Harris vs Trump, 50-50.

The other America is:

Trump 60%+.

The latter world is better suited for screenshots.

More suitable for forwarding.

More suitable for creating emotions.

It is more suitable to become a sentence:

The market knows.

This is why prediction markets spread better than polls.

Polls are complicated.

sample size.

weighted.

State level model.

margin of error.

likely voters.

registered voters.

A whole bunch of methodologies.

Polymarket Not required.

a number:

67%.

end.

For the first time, politics was reduced to something resembling a stock ticker.

And what the modern Internet likes most is this kind of thing.

Because it’s simple.

Fast.

Screenshots are available.

Can spread.

Can be emotional.

5. What’s really ridiculous: a Frenchman almost bought the “Trump will win” narrative

In October 2024, people began to notice a batch of huge Trump bets.

Multiple accounts continue to buy Trump.

The scale is so large that the market begins to doubt:

Is someone deliberately pushing up Trump’s winning rate?

Polymarket later said that a French trader was actually behind these large accounts and said it had found no evidence of his intent to manipulate the market. The relevant Trump positions are extremely large.

The most noteworthy aspect of this matter is not:

Did the French manipulate American politics?

There is no public evidence to prove this.

And in the end Trump really won.

Judging from the results, he can even reasonably say:

I just judged it right before you did.

But the problem is:

He bought more than a contract.

He is also affecting a probability that the whole world is watching.

Let’s say one day Trump is 55%.

He buys it.

57%.

Keep buying.

60%.

Media reports:

“Trump leads the prediction market by a wide margin.”

And then supporters see that.

traders see.

Wall Street sees it.

More people are starting to do the so-called Trump trade.

The price of Trump continues to rise.

You will suddenly find:

A market that is supposed to be responsible for “reflecting” political reality,

Start participating in creating political reality.

This is the most critical step.

6. Polymarket’s Trump probability later really entered Wall Street

If Polymarket only affected Crypto Twitter, I wouldn’t say it affected the presidential election.

At most it’s just a coin circle toy.

But what’s really happening in 2024 is:

Expectations of Trump’s victory began to enter traditional asset prices.

USD.

U.S. debt.

Bitcoin.

Trump Media.

RMB.

Mexican peso.

interest rate.

The so-called “Trump trade” has quickly become one of the most important trading themes on Wall Street.

Reuters reported in late October that part of the reason for the strength of the U.S. dollar was that the market began to increase expectations for Trump’s victory; the report also specifically mentioned that although polls still show Trump and Harris are very close, there has been a significant increase in Trump victory betting on Polymarket.

On November 1, Reuters reported that hedge funds began to look for trades that could profit from Trump’s victory, and clearly pointed out that some betting websites’ preference for Trump has provided momentum to “Trump trades”.

A similar phenomenon is even occurring in the interest rate options market. At the end of October, Reuters reported that U.S. interest rate options began to price in a Republican victory and higher volatility. The article directly mentioned that as Trump’s victory rate increased in online markets such as Polymarket, related transactions began to be promoted.

Notice what’s going on here.

Polymarket:

Trump may win.

↓

Trader:

Then I buy Trump-benefiting assets.

↓

Asset prices rise.

↓

Media:

“The Trump trade is heating up.”

↓

Public:

Wall Street also thinks Trump will win.

↓

The Trump “is winning” narrative continues to grow.

This is no longer a simple prediction platform.

It became:

Expected upstream.

7. Trump Media itself has become a presidential lottery

Before the 2024 election, Trump Media’s stock price is highly tied to Trump’s probability of winning.

Reuters later reported that in the six weeks before Trump won the election, Trump Media’s stock price rose by about 196%; investors increasingly regarded the stock as a proxy asset for Trump’s political prospects.

Even on election night, some Trump Media supporters looked at stock prices and Polymarket’s Trump odds while watching the real election results.

This scene is very interesting.

Politics.

stocks.

Gambling.

Cryptocurrency.

media.

Already completely mixed together.

Are you supporting the presidential candidate?

Or are you trading assets?

You’re watching the election;

Still looking at the odds?

You are judging politics,

Or are you judging how others will judge politics?

Modern politics has become a real-time trading terminal.

And Polymarket is right in the center of the screen.

8. This is what Polymarket really gives Trump: Momentum

What is Trump best at?

Not policy details.

Not an academic argument.

Instead:

momentum.

A sense of winning.

crowd.

heat.

Unstoppable.

“Everyone is talking about me.”

“I have the biggest rally.”

“I have the highest approval rating.”

“They’re all targeting me.”

“I’m winning.”

This narrative itself is part of Trump’s political style.

And Polymarket gives this political style an almost perfect financial expression.

No need to shout:

Trump is winning.

Just show:

Trump 64%.

The effect is even stronger.

Because it doesn’t look like a slogan.

It’s data.

The most important thing is:

It is data updated in real time.

Trump says a word.

The odds move.

The debate is over.

The odds move.

An assassination occurs.

The odds move.

Biden withdraws from the race.

The odds move.

Harris accepted the nomination.

The odds move.

Trump is no longer just a candidate.

He became a K-line.

This is a natural fit for politicians like Trump who rely heavily on attention and momentum.

9. Then Elon Musk helped Polymarket complete the communication

In the 2024 election, there is another person who cannot be ignored:

Elon Musk.

He openly supports Trump.

At the same time, he is also one of the most communicative people in the world.

Reuters reported in the lead-up to the election that Musk believed betting markets were more accurate than polls because real money was in them.

The spread of this sentence is extremely lethal.

Because it changes prediction market from:

“Gambler’s stuff”

Upgraded to:

“The way smart people see the real world.”

So a narrative that is extremely suitable for the Trump camp emerged:

Traditional media cannot be trusted.

The polls cannot be trusted.

Experts cannot be trusted.

But the market is credible.

Why?

Because:

people have skin in the game.

This is almost the financial version of MAGA’s distrust of the establishment.

As a result, there is a natural ideological resonance between Polymarket and Trump.

Not because Polymarket officials said:

Vote Trump.

But because it provides a narrative language that is very suitable for Trump:

Don’t believe them. Look at the price.

10. This is why traditional polls will appear so weak in 2024

The real problem with traditional polls is not necessarily “inaccuracy.”

But it lost to the prediction market in communication.

The poll said:

48.1% vs 46.7%.

Error range ±3%.

Swing state statistical error.

The model has turnout assumption.

Ordinary people read:

Don’t know.

Polymarket:

Trump 62%.

Ordinary people read:

Trump is winning.

So the prediction market is not won by statistics.

What it won was:

Narrative efficiency.

This is very important.

Because modern politics is not conducted in papers.

It’s done on the phone screen.

The information that is easiest to understand is often the most powerful information.

And the probability of a real-time jump,

Naturally, it is more suitable for the mobile Internet than dozens of pages of polling methodology.

11. Polymarket even makes Trump’s election expectations “tradable”

In the past, “I think Trump will win” was just an opinion.

In 2024, this view is suddenly tradable.

Do you think Trump wins?

Buy Trump.

Do you think Trump’s coming to power will push Bitcoin higher?

Buy Bitcoin.

Do you think tariffs will push the dollar higher?

Buy dollars.

Do you think the yuan will come under pressure?

Short the RMB.

Do you think Trump will be good for his company?

Buy DJT.

So what’s most noteworthy about 2024 isn’t:

Everyone started predicting Trump.

Instead:

The entire financial system started trading Trump.

Polymarket plays a very special role in this.

It provides the simplest anchor:

Trump win probability.

This probability becomes a reference for many other asset narratives.

Once the probability of Trump increases,

The “Trump trade” is easier to justify.

And once the Trump trade really goes up,

It will be further strengthened:

The market believes Trump will win.

This is a very beautiful self-reinforcing structure.

12. Some people will say: These people already support Trump.

Of course.

This is the most logical place to refute this article.

Polymarket’s user base is already highly crypto-native.

In 2024, Trump openly embraced cryptocurrency, which was more popular among many currency users than the Democratic camp.

Before the election, Reuters quoted industry insiders as warning: Polymarket may be dominated by crypto-native users, and these users themselves are more Trump-biased, so prices may not be representative of ordinary American voters.

This is absolutely correct.

But if you think about it, it makes things more interesting.

If Polymarket is just “Trump-biased currency circles betting on themselves”,

Why do CNN, Reuters, Bloomberg, and Wall Street traders still watch it?

Because once the price is big enough,

It starts to break away from the original user base.

Something doesn’t need to perfectly represent voters;

To influence voters to understand reality.

Twitter is also not representative of the U.S. population.

Media reporters also do not represent the U.S. population.

Wall Street is even less representative of the U.S. population.

But they can still define political narratives.

The power of Polymarket is not:

It represents every constituent.

Instead:

It succeeded in getting important people to watch it.

13. So did Polymarket help Trump get even one more vote?

Don’t know.

There is no reliable public evidence to tell you:

“Polymarket gave Trump X million more votes.”

There is not enough evidence to prove:

If Polymarket hadn’t existed, Harris would have won.

So if you understand the title as a strict statistical causal proposition:

“Without Polymarket, Trump would never have won the presidency.”

This cannot be proven.

It may even be overly exaggerated.

But political influence cannot always be reduced to:

How many votes to add.

Imagine a few questions:

Has Polymarket helped reinforce the feeling that Trump is “winning”?

Yes.

Have Polymarket probabilities been cited by mainstream media?

Yes.

Has it entered the information environment of Trump trade on Wall Street?

Yes.

Have the huge bets sparked a discussion about whether Trump odds are being pushed up?

Yes.

Does it provide Trump supporters with a very useful communication tool?

Apparently there is.

Then there is only one question left:

Do you think “who looks like he’s going to win” has any impact on politics?

If the answer is yes,

Well Polymarket is already involved in the election.

14. Trump himself is the person who best understands the value of “looking like a winner”

Trump’s entire political career is built on a very simple brand:

WINNING.

winner.

Success.

Max.

Best.

First.

Everyone is looking at me.

Everyone is talking about me.

Everyone thought I was going to win.

For such a politician,

Polymarket is almost a God-sent tool.

Because Polymarket puts:

“Trump is winning”

became:

Trump: 67%

Trump doesn’t even have to say it himself.

Let a “market” speak for him.

This is so much more advanced than a campaign ad.

You know campaign ads are propaganda.

Prediction markets are not.

At least it doesn’t seem like it.

So the political propaganda completed an upgrade:

Opinion disguised as probability.

15. If there is no Polymarket, what will Trump lose in 2024?

Certainly not the ballot itself.

What is missing is a very important one:

Momentum Machine.

One keeps telling the internet:

Trump is more likely to win

machine.

There is no Polymarket,

There are also betting sites.

And Kalshi.

There are also traditional markets.

And there are polls.

Trump could still win, of course.

Maybe even still win.

But without Polymarket, the political information landscape of 2024 will be missing something very symbolic:

A huge, real-time, globally traded, screenshot-capable Trump win probability.

This is why the title should deliberately be more absolute:

Without Polymarket, Trump would not have become president.

What it really wants to express is not:

Polymarket stole the election.

Instead:

Trump becoming president has already happened in the market before there are votes.

16. What’s even more terrifying is: this machine will never disappear.

Trump is just the first person to really push the prediction market into a presidential political narrative.

But it won’t be the last one.

Every future presidential election:

Candidate probability.

Swing state probabilities.

Congress controls the odds.

Vice Presidential Pick.

Debate performance.

Probability of withdrawal.

judicial cases.

Policy adoption rate.

will be traded in real time.

Politics will become more and more like financial markets.

A piece of news comes out.

Market repricing.

Reporter repricing.

Candidate response repricing.

Traders continue trading.

Then the reporter reports on it.

At a certain stage,

We may not even be able to tell the difference:

The market is predicting politics,

Or does politics start to revolve around market prices.

This is where Polymarket really changed American politics.

It didn’t elect Trump.

Instead it lets:

“Who will become president?”

It became an asset that could be traded 24 hours a day.

Once the president himself can be priced,

The presidential election is no longer just a civic act.

It simultaneously becomes:

financial products.

Media products.

Traffic products.

Speculative products.

17. Finally, back to the most ridiculous title

Without Polymarket,

Will Trump win?

History has happened.

We could never actually perform this experiment.

So no one can prove it.

But ask the other way around:

If there is no Polymarket in 2024,

Will Trump’s victory be missing something extremely important?

The answer is yes.

One less person keeps telling the world:

Trump is winning

real-time price.

One less place for whales, currency circles, media, Musk, traders and ordinary supporters to discuss Trump around the same number.

One less machine that can instantly convert political sentiment into financial prices.

Losing one would mean:

“I support Trump”

Instantly upgraded to:

“The market thinks Trump will win”

narrative tool.

The political power of these two sentences is completely different.

So strictly speaking:

It’s not Polymarket that decides who gets to vote.

It wasn’t Polymarket that counted the votes.

It wasn’t Polymarket that put Trump in the White House.

But it does something that might be more relevant to this era.

It packages Trump into one in advance:

Winners available to buy.

Then Wall Street starts trading on this winner.

The media started reporting on the winner.

Supporters began spreading the word about the winner.

The internet is starting to get used to this winner.

Finally,

Ballots only complete the final step.

That’s why I still prefer to write the title as:

Without Polymarket, Trump Wouldn’t Become President

Because what really happens in 2024 may not be that Polymarket successfully predicted Trump.

But Trump proved one thing for the first time:

In today’s America, to be president, you need more than just winning votes.

You also need to win the market first.
